reflects_period: 2025-2026 (model-year 2025 new prices; used = about 3-5 years old)

basis.prices_and_economy: Typical new MSRP bands, used-market (Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book, NADA) values and EPA fueleconomy.gov combined ratings for representative models, rounded; marine and off-road from manufacturer spec sheets (Mercury, Yamaha, Sea-Doo, Polaris, Honda) and dealer pricing.
basis.insurance: Bankrate / Insurify 2025 average premiums: full coverage about $2,300-$2,700 per year for a clean-record adult, state-minimum liability about $600-$800 per year; EVs are 15-25% higher; boats about 1.5% of value per year; rounded to cents per month.
basis.maintenance: Manufacturer service schedules and AAA / RepairPal cost surveys, rounded.
basis.registration: State DMV fee ranges; actual cost varies by weight, value, age and county.

unit_conventions.mi_per_kwh: miles per kilowatt-hour of usable battery energy
unit_conventions.gal_per_hour: US gallons per hour of engine run time
unit_conventions.tank_capacity: Usable fuel in US gallons (also given in liters).
unit_conventions.cargo_l: Cargo volume in liters (road: usually seats-folded for SUVs and minivans; boats and ATVs: storage plus racks).
unit_conventions.payload_kg: Maximum payload including passengers, in kilograms.
unit_conventions.towing_kg: Maximum rated towing capacity in kilograms (0 if not rated).

road.basis: Multipliers on fuel (or energy) consumed per mile relative to the combined rating; >1 burns more. Rounded rules of thumb from EPA/fueleconomy.gov and AAA tests.
road.ev_note: For EVs the same multipliers apply to kWh per mile (cold weather is harsher: use 1.35; highway 75 mph: 1.30; towing: 2.0).

marine.basis: Multipliers on gallons per hour at planing cruise; rules of thumb from engine makers' fuel curves (Mercury, Yamaha, Volvo Penta) and BoatUS guidance.
marine.note: Plan on the 1/3 out, 1/3 back, 1/3 reserve fuel rule. Marine tank capacities are usable gallons.

offroad.basis: Multipliers on gallons per hour at normal trail pace; rule-of-thumb values from OEM spec sheets and trail-riding reports.

air.basis: Multipliers on gallons per hour at normal cruise; rules of thumb from light-aircraft operating handbooks' fuel tables and flight-school planning guidance.
air.note: Plan a 30-minute day VFR reserve (45 minutes at night) on top of the trip's fuel.

fields.fuel_type: gasoline | diesel | electricity | avgas (aviation gasoline) | none (pedalled, paddled or rowed).
fields.consumption: Rate by unit; road gives city/highway/combined, marine and off-road give gallons per hour by regime.
fields.range_miles_typical: Approximate range on a full tank or battery at combined consumption.
fields.range_hours_typical: Approximate engine hours on a full tank at the "normal/cruise" rate.
fields.price_used_cents: Integer cents {min, typical, max}; about 3-5 years old (boats and off-road: 3-7).
fields.insurance_cents_per_month: Integer cents per month for a clean-record adult: state-minimum liability and full coverage (liability + collision/comprehensive).
fields.maintenance: Intervals in miles or hours and an annual cost in cents; null interval = not applicable.
fields.registration_cents_per_year: Integer cents per year {min, typical, max}.
fields.consumption_factors_ref: Pointer to the multiplier guide for terrain/load.
fields.aliases: Other words a purchase or a story names one of the class by ("pickup", "jet ski"), lowercase; the longest that matches wins.
fields.make: A representative make for a new one of the class, as a picker suggests it.
fields.model: A representative model of that make.
fields.fuel_cents_per_gal: Integer cents per US gallon of the class's fuel where the price catalog has no row for it (aviation gasoline).

entries.name: Compact car (Civic / Corolla class)
entries.notes: US new-vehicle average transaction price is near $49,000 in 2025 across all classes; compacts are at the low end.

entries.name: Midsize sedan (Camry / Accord class)
entries.notes: Hybrid variants reach 45-52 mpg combined.

entries.name: Midsize pickup (Tacoma / Colorado class)
entries.notes: Cargo is the open bed (about 5 ft). Towing about 6,500 lb.

entries.name: Full-size pickup (F-150 / Silverado class)
entries.notes: Cargo is the open bed (5.5-6.5 ft). Towing up to ~10,000 lb with the right package.

entries.name: Heavy-duty diesel pickup (2500 / F-250 class)
entries.notes: DEF fluid (diesel exhaust fluid) refills every ~5,000 miles, about $15-25/ 2.5 gal. Towing up to 15,000-20,000 lb.

entries.name: Compact SUV (RAV4 / CR-V class)
entries.notes: Cargo volume is with the rear seats folded: about 1,100 L; behind seats about 540 L. Hybrids reach 38-41 mpg.

entries.name: Midsize three-row SUV (Highlander / Explorer class)
entries.notes: Cargo with second and third rows folded about 2,300 L; behind the third row about 480 L.

entries.name: Minivan (Sienna / Odyssey / Pacifica class)
entries.notes: Hybrid minivans (Sienna) return 35-36 mpg combined; cargo with rows folded is about 4,000 L (140 cu ft).

entries.name: Electric sedan (Model 3 / Ioniq 6 class)
entries.notes: No oil changes. Many states add an EV registration surcharge of about $100-$250 per year, included in the registration band. Tires wear faster (instant torque, weight).

entries.name: Electric crossover (Model Y / Equinox EV class)
entries.notes: Cargo volume with rear seats folded.

entries.name: Motorcycle, standard or cruiser (500-900 cc)
entries.notes: Cargo is saddlebags or a tail bag; a passenger seat is optional. Front/rear tires are replaced separately (rear wears ~2x faster). Helmet laws vary by state.

entries.name: Scooter or moped (50-150 cc)
entries.notes: Under-seat storage about 25-35 L. Mopeds under 50 cc often need no registration or license in some states; top speed 30-60 mph.

entries.name: Outboard bass boat (18-20 ft, 150-200 hp)

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil, filters and lower-unit gear oil every 100 hours or annually

entries.notes: Boat state registration usually renews every 1-3 years (annualised here); trailer is registered separately (~$30-$100/year). Price includes motor and trailer. Cruise burn is at planing speed with a normal load.

entries.name: Pontoon boat (22-24 ft, 90-150 hp outboard)
entries.notes: Capacity plate typically 8-13 persons / 1,500-2,500 lb total.

entries.name: Personal watercraft / jet ski (1-3 seats)

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil and filter every 50 hours or annually

entries.notes: Premium-grade fuel recommended by most makers. Price excludes trailer ($800-$2,500).

entries.name: Cruising sailboat with auxiliary diesel (30-35 ft)

consumption.note: Displacement hull: motors at hull speed (~6 knots) burning 0.6-1.0 gph; sailing uses no fuel.

maintenance.engine_service_note: oil and filters every 100-150 hours; impeller every 200 hours

entries.notes: Documented vessels (US Coast Guard documentation) pay no state registration. A rule of thumb is that ownership costs 10% of value per year. Sleeps 4-6.

entries.name: ATV, utility quad (450-700 cc)
entries.notes: Cargo: front and rear racks, about 40 kg front and 80 kg rear. Many states require an off-highway vehicle (OHV) sticker/permit rather than road registration; helmet and age rules vary.

entries.name: UTV / side-by-side (Ranger / RZR class, 2-4 seats)
entries.notes: Utility models carry a dump bed up to ~450 kg; sport models carry people only. Roll cage and belts required.

entries.name: Dirt bike, 250 cc four-stroke
entries.notes: Competition bikes are not street legal; plated dual-sport bikes use the motorcycle class. Premium fuel with 91+ octane typical.

entries.name: Bicycle (commuter, hybrid or mountain bike)
entries.notes: Pedalled: no fuel, so no range; a shop tune-up stands in for the service. Most US states register none; homeowners or renters insurance usually covers theft.

entries.name: Electric bicycle (Class 1-3 e-bike)
entries.notes: Pedal-assist to 20 mph (Class 1-2) or 28 mph (Class 3); a few states register or plate Class 3.

entries.name: Cargo van (Transit / Sprinter / ProMaster class)
entries.notes: High-roof, long-wheelbase vans hold about 15 m3; commercial use raises the premium.

entries.name: Box truck (16-26 ft, Class 6 diesel)
entries.notes: Under 26,001 lb GVWR, so no CDL needed; commercial insurance and an annual DOT inspection.

entries.name: Semi tractor (Class 8 sleeper, diesel)
entries.notes: Needs a Class A CDL; registration is apportioned (IRP) by the miles run in each state. Payload is the cab's; the trailer is towed.

entries.name: Bus (school bus or shuttle, diesel)
entries.notes: Carrying 16 or more people needs a CDL with a passenger endorsement.

entries.name: Motorhome (Class C or Class A RV)
entries.notes: Sleeps four to eight; propane, fresh-water and holding tanks are its own upkeep.

entries.name: Snowmobile (600-850 cc, trail)
entries.notes: Snow only: a trail permit or registration is required in snowbelt states.

entries.name: Farm tractor (utility, 45-100 hp diesel)
entries.notes: Farm use usually needs no registration; on public roads it carries a slow-moving-vehicle sign.

entries.name: Rowboat or jon boat (10-14 ft, oars)
entries.notes: Rowed: no fuel. Most states register a hull only once an outboard is fitted.

entries.name: Kayak or canoe (paddled, 1-2 seats)
entries.notes: Paddled: no fuel. A few states ask for a launch permit or an invasive-species sticker.

entries.name: Small plane (four-seat single piston, Cessna 172 class)
entries.notes: Flown by a licensed pilot between airfields; FAA registration lasts seven years, and some states add an aircraft fee or tax. Hangar or tie-down rent is extra.

entries.name: Light helicopter (four-seat piston, Robinson R44 class)
entries.notes: Lands at a helipad, an airfield or any cleared spot the route names; the rotor and engine overhaul come due together at about 2,200 hours.
